newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland seeks new bid for air tracking system.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland seeks new bid for air tracking system.

text.p: Two consortiums competing for a contract to build a 650 million Swiss franc airspace tracking system for Switzerland have agreed to produce a third, joint proposal for the project, the defence ministry said on Thursday.

The two consortiums, one comprising Hughes Aircraft Co and Siemens AG's Swiss unit and the other comprising Thomson-CSF and Contraves, a unit of Oerlikon-Buehrle Holding AG, had already submitted separate proposals for the military tracking system in April.
But in June the ministry asked the two groups to produce a third, combined proposal with the aim of providing another option in the government's search for the best price/performance alternative.
The two consortiums last week agreed to produce a joint proposal, to be submitted by early September, defence department spokesman Bruno Frangi said.
The separate proposalse submitted by the two groups in April remain valid, the ministry also said in a statement.
The ministry's 1998 budget earmarks 450 million to 500 million francs for the so-called Florako system with the rest of the funding to come in a subsequent budget.
The system will replace the current outmoded system in phases from the year 2001. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
